Job Description:

Aims Community College actively supports an environment that embraces the College's Mission, Vision, Values and a culture of innovation and care. The College embraces and seeks to hire individuals who want to be a part of this environment and have the skill sets necessary to be successful in this position.

The Director II, CARE Case Management, oversees and provides direction for the CARE department and its team. This role provides leadership, direct supervision, and guidance to CARE case managers and assists the Executive Director with strategic planning, program development, training, and assessment. Additionally, the Director ensures compliance with case management and operational excellence.

This position involves delivering non-clinical, goal-oriented, and strengths-based assessments, interventions, and service coordination for students facing challenges in health, housing, finances, academics, behavior, and overall well-being. The Director is responsible for immediate problem-solving in both traditional and complex situations, identifying resources, making referrals, and offering basic-needs support to enhance student success and holistic wellness. Through a coordinated and integrated approach, this role collaborates closely with other offices, particularly Counseling, and third-party agencies to connect students with resources that promote their success, ensuring equitable support for all students across various locations and modalities. This position will also collaborate with the Behavioral Intervention Team (BIT) to address varying levels of distress and risk and connect students to appropriate resources.

Some travel may be required for this position.

Non-Clinical Case Management: 40%

  • Schedules and conducts intake appointments to assess students' needs holistically and create an action plan for support.
  • Delivers individualized CARE and case management services, including resource management, service planning, and monitoring/evaluation.
  • Teaches students problem-solving techniques and guides them in identifying alternative options related to their goals.
  • Maintains accurate case notes in the electronic record-keeping system, reflecting essential information and discussions.
  • Refers students to relevant on-campus and community resources based on their needs.
  • Establishes and maintains partnerships with community agencies to address students' basic needs.
  • Serves as the initial point of contact for students seeking services in the CARE and counseling office.

Leadership & Supervision: 30%

  • Supervise support staff overseeing and directing daily operations, providing guidance and performance management, and ensuring efficient team productivity.
  • Offers leadership, guidance, and support in case management practices and professional development.
  • Assists in the training and onboarding of new case managers, ensuring adherence to and compliance with best practices and institutional policies.

CARE Departmental Leadership: 20%

  • This position is responsible for overseeing and directing all CARE related services, programs, and staff. This role is the leader within the CARE department and serves as the direct contact for escalated complex situations.
  • Participates and directs assessment efforts related to case management effectiveness.
  • Supports the Executive Director in strategic planning, program evaluation and assessment, and reporting.
  • Collaborates with the Executive Director to develop and implement strategies to improve program effectiveness.
  • Maintains knowledge of community and campus resources by ongoing engagement with Aims faculty and staff, public health, private services, and community stakeholders.
  • Evaluates and enhances the quality of case management services through consistent assessment, detailed documentation, comprehensive reporting, and the proactive revision of policies and procedures.
  • Directs, oversees, and supports case management staff in achieving and maintaining relevant professional development certifications and engaging in continuous training.
  • Designs, develops, and implements educational programs to advance case management practices and knowledge both at the department level and college-wide level.
  • Leads weekly case management meetings, ensuring continuity and effective team collaboration.
  • This role supports the Behavioral Intervention Team (BIT) by determining who is referred to the BIT for additional interventions.
  • Contributes to BIT Team discussions and assessments using case notes and referral information.
  • Implements and directs BIT Team-recommended interventions and support plans for students.
  • Conducts an initial generalized risk assessment of BIT referrals using the NABITA Risk Rubric and shares those results with the Dean of Student Engagement and Inclusion.
  • Provides budget development recommendations to the Executive Director.
  • Adheres to internal compliance standards and ensures support staff is also in compliance with case management practices.

Prevention & Well-Being Programming: 5%

  • Directs the development and implementation of educational materials, support groups, and wellness programming tailored to common basic needs.
  • Creates and directs marketing and awareness campaigns promoting case management services.
  • Conducts training sessions for faculty and staff on effectively supporting students with basic needs.
  • Collaborates with the ED, SAWB to develop an ongoing CARE program training series for case managers.
  • Develops and directs the annual CARE program training series for faculty and staff.
  • Directs and provides programming opportunities for students related to mental health and wellness.
  • Directs and develops curriculum for student workshops on mental health topics across all satellite campuses.

Other Duties as Assigned: 5%


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field; plus four (4) years of related experience which must include direct service to students or an equivalent combination of education and/or work experience. Of the required four (4) years of experience, two (2) years must be supervisory and/or demonstrated leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated high interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively and equitably with diverse populations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work collegially and collaboratively with supervisors and colleagues.
  • Demonstrated ability to make decisions and take action on those decisions.
  • Ability to manage departments with high-volume workflows.

REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO UPLOAD:

  • Cover Letter
  • Resume

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in case management or coordinating services within a higher education setting.
  • Familiarity with student information systems (e.g., Workday) and case management databases (e.g., Maxient).
  • Experience making professional presentations to groups of up to 50 people.
  • Experience working with a diverse student population, including post-traditional students, students of color, Veterans, first-generation college students, and others from underserved or underrepresented backgrounds.
  • Working knowledge of mental health, student development, BIT best practices, higher education law, FERPA, and electronic record-keeping systems.
  • Experience responding to students in crisis, including using de-escalation strategies, coordinating with campus and community partners, and connecting students to appropriate support.
  • Experience coordinating welfare checks, conducting suicide risk assessments, and developing, documenting, and monitoring risk management plans for students of concern.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish)

All Applicants:

  • Compare your previous work experience to the job duties listed on the job positing under job description. Enter the job duties you have performed under the "Work Experience" section on your job application. We evaluate your experience based on this information.
  • Please make sure you state whether work experience (aka work history) is part time or full time employment by listing the average number of hours worked per week. This information is used to determine your new annual salary.
  • Be sure to upload all the required documents listed at the above in "Additional Job Description" section. This can be uploaded as part of your application materials in the "My Experience" section.  If there are missing documents, your incomplete application will not be considered. Per the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, you may redact information that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

For information on our hiring practices, please visit our resource page: https://www.aims.edu/departments/human-resources/hiring-process.

Aims Community College is an equal opportunity employer.  Selection will be based solely on merit and will be without discrimination based on age, ancestry, color, creed, disability, ethnicity, familial status, gender, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, race, religion, or veteran's status.  All application materials must be submitted by the closing date posted and become the property of Aims Community College. The screening committee will select finalists for interviews. The goal of Aims Community College is to enhance the diversity present in the district we serve. To comply with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, if hired, you will be required to provide documents within three (3) business days of hire date to show your identity and your authorization to work. This law applies to all persons hired.

Screening/Selection:

To be considered, please provide a thorough and complete application. Initial screening will be conducted by a committee based on completed application materials.

Employees in these positions may be asked to participate in temporary assignments lasting less than nine (9) months (such as curriculum development, short term projects, meetings and substitute duties) which could amount to additional temporary pay.

Upon hire, all positions at Aims Community College require a criminal background check and may require industry specific screenings such as an MVR, physical and/or drug screen. Keep in mind, a conviction does not automatically preclude candidates from being employed. The nature of a conviction will be considered relative to the duties of the position.
